absent: Definitions and full layouts of task descriptor, runqueue, root domain, scheduler class, scheduler domain and extensible scheduler objects beyond fields touched here.
Implementation and contracts of fallback CPU selection, task migration, pinned task detection and hotplug wait primitives.
Trigger conditions and callers for online offline transitions, CPU activation and forced address space initialization.
Ordering and sleep ability rules for scheduler class online offline hooks.
Exact semantics of symmetric threading mask, frozen task flag and active CPU set maintenance.
Behavior of extensible scheduler operations for online offline, idle topology effects and exit handling beyond dispatch decision.
Processing side of capacity synchronization and kick work execution.
Allocation ownership and lifetime for NUMA distance tables, masks and topology levels.
Export status and stable ABI guarantees for any symbol in these fragments.
Configuration conditions selecting alternate empty definitions versus full definitions.

findings.text: A scheduler interface updates the preferred NUMA node recorded for a target task. The update preserves queue placement across the change and completes while holding task runqueue protection.
Modification of the preferred NUMA preference requires holding the task runqueue lock together with a scheduler change guard that saves dequeue state. No other ordering is shown in the fragment.

Runqueue online management exposes operations to mark a runqueue online or offline and locked wrappers that validate root domain membership before delegating. Online marking joins the shared online set before notifying scheduling classes, while offline marking notifies classes before leaving the set after refreshing the runqueue clock.

Online and offline transitions are guarded by the current online flag so repeated requests have no effect. The shared online set and the flag change together in each direction, and class notification only occurs on an actual transition.

CPU activation clears any push offload callback, accounts for symmetric threading presence, marks the CPU active, refreshes NUMA and cpuset state when symmetric multiprocessing initialization has completed, notifies the extensible scheduler layer, then ensures the runqueue is online. The routine always reports success in the fragment.

Installation or removal of the push offload callback and the online offline wrappers acquire the runqueue lock with interrupt state saved. The push offload routine itself requires the caller to already hold the runqueue lock.

During CPU teardown the scheduler keeps a persistent push callback installed on the outgoing runqueue. Per CPU threads and migration disabled tasks are left in place, with a wake of the hotplug waiter when nothing runnable or pinned remains and a waiter is present. Otherwise the current task reference is retained, the runqueue lock is temporarily released with preemption and interrupts still disabled to request a stopper execution, then reacquired with rescheduling pending so the stopper runs next and moves the task to a fallback CPU when it is still queued on the same runqueue.

Alternate definitions provide empty behavior for push offload control, hotplug waiting, extensible scheduler activation, capacity seeding, and NUMA refresh. Their presence indicates build configurations where the corresponding feature is disabled.

Extensible scheduler activation for a runqueue delegates to a hotplug handler with an online indication. The handler obtains the protected root scheduler object and advances a global hotplug sequence before any further work.

The hotplug handler refreshes idle selection topology when the extensible scheduler is active, reseeds or clears per CPU capacity state according to direction, translates CPU identity through a table when identifier type requires it while updating online masks under scheduler lock, then invokes the online or offline operation when available. When neither applicable operation is present the handler terminates the scheduler with a hotplug restart reason.

Idle CPU selection optimizations for cache and NUMA locality are enabled only when the corresponding domain weight of the first online CPU is positive but smaller than the total online count. NUMA optimization additionally requires a mismatch between cache and NUMA weights across online CPUs and requires that per node builtin idle is not requested. Domain weights read zero and spans read absent when the underlying domain or group is missing.

Topology weight and span queries run under read side protection for scheduler domains, with an explicit read lock held across the combined selection update. Retrieval of the scheduler root requires either the CPU set read lock or the enable mutex to be held.

Online capacity seeding walks scheduler descendants in preorder under runqueue protection, skipping the root which never uses the relevant state, and under each shard lock queues at most one synchronization request per CPU which triggers a remote kick when newly queued. Offline clearing walks the same hierarchy and resets the per CPU values.

Kick requests disable local interrupts while updating per CPU kick sets and queuing interrupt work. The idle variant attempts the target runqueue lock without blocking to test whether a kick can be skipped, releasing the observation through a helper that validates lock ownership and advances a drop sequence when core scheduling is enabled.

Kick requests issued from nonmaskable interrupt context are rejected with an error report and have no effect. Requests issued while bypassing for power management on the local CPU are silently suppressed to avoid malfunction of deferred work during impaired interrupt handling.

An idle kick may be skipped only when the target runqueue current task is not the idle task and the runqueue is not flagged as inside dispatch. Checking current alone is insufficient because a remote pull may still fail and leave the runqueue idle.

Observed runqueue state includes an online flag, a CPU identifier, a root domain pointer with span and online sets, a runnable count, a persistent balance callback pointer, a hotplug wait object, a current task pointer, and extensible scheduler substate for flags, kick lists, work items and synchronization lists. Scheduler class hooks for online and offline transitions are optional.

Forced initialization of memory management state switches the current context to the initial address space when it is elsewhere, grabbing a reference beforehand and dropping the old reference after switching with interrupts disabled and post switch architecture handling. The fragment notes that boot CPU finalization cleans related state.

Scheduler NUMA topology refresh occurs only when the affected node contains exactly one CPU, treating that as first online or last offline, and otherwise leaves state unchanged. Initialization records base and possibly modified distance tables, publishes distance and level state with appropriate ordering, builds per level per node masks of CPUs within each distance threshold, warns once on asymmetric distances when verbose debugging is enabled, then extends the default topology with a node identity level plus additional NUMA levels and records the resulting level count and topology type.

Topology initialization returns early without further publication when any required allocation fails, leaving previously published state as is. Distance asymmetry warnings print a full matrix distinguishing nodes without CPUs and occur at most once per boot.

Queuing of capacity synchronization relies on the shard lock to exclude concurrent attempts for the same identifier and pairs a full barrier with the processing side so either the list check observes absence and queues or the in flight processing observes the earlier update.

Suspend resume accounting maintains a counter of frozen CPUs. Entering frozen state increments the counter and resets domains, while leaving decrements and only on the last online restores full cpuset domains before updating active sets. Outside frozen operation active sets are updated directly.
